To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we derive a new class of concentration inequalities for the eigenvalues of a kernel matrix; (2) the concentration inequalities are derived under the assumption of a regularity condition on the kernel; and (3) the regularity condition is well-suited to study the eigenvalues of kernel matrices arising from random geometric graphs.

1) we derive concentration inequalities on the spectrum of a random kernel matrix; 2) we study random geometric graphs in a metric space and show how our results apply to them; 3) we give explicit formulas for the fluctuations of the spectrum of a geometric graph.

1) we derive concentration inequalities that quantify the deviation of the spectrum of a random matrix with respect to the eigenvalues of an associated integral operators; 2) we study random geometric graphs, giving explicit formulas and concentration results for the spectrum; and 3) we show that the regularity of a kernel is related to the decay of its eigenvalues.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the regularity of a kernel function can be used to obtain concentration bounds on the spectrum of the associated kernel matrix, even if the kernel is not positive definite.
, in the absence of positive definiteness, the spectrum of a random kernel matrix can still be concentrated around a deterministic limit, and that this limit can be explicitly computed.
